evidence.title: Star Carr & North Sea Wetlands (Britain–Doggerland): Early Mesolithic lake-edge camps
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon-dated birch timber platforms, stag-antler frontlets and Maglemosian microlithic peat deposits across post-glacial northern basins.
evidence.summary: Documents rapid Early Holocene re-occupation of warming temperate wetlands, birch-bark resin hafting, timber lakeside walkways and hunting-foraging across Britain before North Sea submergence.
evidence.limits: Peat drainage and offshore North Sea inundation restrict recovery of contemporary coastal base camps.

evidence.title: Duvensee Bog & Boreal Hazelnut–Pine Woodlands (Northern Europe): Specialized Mesolithic storage
evidence.dateBasis: Waterlogged pine-bark hut floors, charred Corylus hazelnut roasting hearths and microlithic flint knapping scatters across Schleswig–Baltic mire basins.
evidence.summary: Demonstrates structured seasonal hazelnut harvesting and birch–pine wetland base camps bridging Boreal temperate reforestation across northern Europe before Ertebølle shell middens.
evidence.limits: Peatland preservation highlights specialized autumn nut-processing islets rather than year-round upland trails.

evidence.title: Lepenski Vir & Iron Gates Gorge (Danube): Fisher-forager limestone architecture & Neolithic shift
evidence.dateBasis: High-resolution AMS radiocarbon Bayesian models on trapezoidal plaster-floored houses, engraved sandstone boulders and burials.
evidence.summary: Reveals semi-sedentary Danube whirlpool sturgeon fishers erecting trapezoidal plastered dwellings and sculpted river-boulder art before integrating Aegean–Anatolian farming packages and incomers.
evidence.limits: Submergence behind the Iron Gates hydroelectric dam confines fieldwork to legacy excavation archives.

evidence.title: Franchthi Cave & Thessalian Plain (Greece): Aegean seafaring to first European farming villages
evidence.dateBasis: Stratified Melos obsidian, deep-sea tunny bones, early domesticated einkorn/sheep and ancient DNA from Aegean Neolithic pioneers.
evidence.summary: Captures continuous transition from Mesolithic maritime Aegean foraging to densely settled Early Neolithic mudbrick tells cultivating Near Eastern crops and caprines.
evidence.limits: Submerged coastal shelves mask several initial shoreline landing camps.

evidence.title: Struma & Maritsa Valleys (Balkans): Starčevo–Karanovo early agropastoral corridors
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon-dated Balkan river-terrace settlements and zooarchaeological assemblages comparing caprine and cattle herd mixes.
evidence.summary: Traces farming dispersal northward through Balkan river corridors where Anatolian crops and livestock adapted from Mediterranean caprines to temperate cattle herding.
evidence.limits: Alluvial burial across valley bottoms complicates regional settlement density counts.

evidence.title: Linearbandkeramik (LBK) Loess Belt (Central Europe): Timber longhouses from Danube to Paris Basin
evidence.dateBasis: Dendrochronology of oak-lined water wells paired with continent-wide radiocarbon and archaeogenetic transects.
evidence.summary: Within centuries, Linear Pottery farmers established post-built timber longhouses across fertile European loess soils from Hungary to France and Ukraine before late-phase fortified enclosures.
evidence.limits: Organic timber posts decay outside deep anoxic wells such as Kückhoven and Altscherbitz.

evidence.title: Impressed & Cardial Sea Corridor (Italy–France–Iberia): Rapid coastal farming dispersal
evidence.dateBasis: Short-lived seed AMS dates and marine-shell-impressed ceramics spanning Adriatic–Tyrrhenian islands to Atlantic Portugal.
evidence.summary: Shows maritime leap-frogging of small domestic flocks and shell-decorated Cardial ceramics along the northern Mediterranean shore, integrating Western Hunter-Gatherer neighbors overland.
evidence.limits: Post-glacial sea-level rise drowned many earliest open-beach anchorage camps.

evidence.title: Ertebølle & Baltic Coastal Foragers (Denmark–N. Germany): Pointed-base pottery & shell middens
evidence.dateBasis: Stratified oyster–cockle kitchen middens, blubber lamps and submerged coastal oak dugouts prior to Funnel Beaker farming.
evidence.summary: Demonstrates prolonged coexistence for over a millennium between agrarian central Europe and productive marine hunter-fisher-potters around Danish fjords before the 4000 BCE Funnel Beaker shift.
evidence.limits: Littorina marine transgressions inundated lower western Baltic settlements.

evidence.title: Megalithic Temples of Malta (Ġgantija, Ħaġar Qim & Mnajdra): Free-standing island stone sanctuaries
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon phasing paired with 3D solar-azimuth simulations across coralline and globigerina limestone apses (UNESCO WHC 132).
evidence.summary: Island farming communities on Malta and Gozo raised massive coralline megalithic temple complexes aligned to solstitial light shafts centuries before continental pyramid building.
evidence.limits: Early nineteenth-century clearings removed key floor deposits inside several temple apses.

evidence.title: Carnac & Morbihan Standing Stones (Brittany): Fifth-millennium Atlantic monumental landscapes
evidence.dateBasis: Excavations at Le Plasker (Plouharnel), Giant Tumuli (Saint-Michel) and alignments inscribed under UNESCO WHC 1725.
evidence.summary: Atlantic Brittany preserves Europe’s earliest grand monumental architecture, combining giant passage-grave mounds, jadeite Alpine axes and kilometer-long stone rows along Morbihan Bay.
evidence.limits: Acidic granite soils dissolve human skeletal bone outside megalithic chamber fills.

evidence.title: Circum-Alpine Pile Dwellings (Switzerland–Lake Garda–Slovenia): Wetland villages & Ötzi’s copper world
evidence.dateBasis: Year-to-year lake-pile oak dendrochronology across 111 transnational Alpine wetland sites (UNESCO WHC 1363).
evidence.summary: Waterlogged lake edges around the Alps preserve textiles, wooden wheels, dugouts and copper-smelting crucibles to sub-annual calendar precision spanning the Neolithic through Hallstatt Iron Age.
evidence.limits: Excavation largely samples submerged littoral villages rather than contemporary dry-land hamlets.

evidence.title: Cucuteni–Trypillia Mega-Sites (Maidanetske & Nebelivka, Ukraine–Romania): Low-density Copper Age cities
evidence.dateBasis: Large-area magnetometry mapping thousands of concentric wattle-and-daub dwellings and assembly halls across 100–320-hectare settlements.
evidence.summary: Concentric planned mega-sites at Maidanetske and Talianki housed thousands of inhabitants around communal assembly buildings and egalitarian neighborhood quarters prior to Mesopotamian-style palaces.
evidence.limits: Periodic ritual house burning and cyclical site abandonment leave population contemporaneity actively researched.

evidence.title: Brú na Bóinne (Newgrange, Ireland) & Atlantic Passage Tombs: Winter solstice architecture
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon-dated passage-tomb kerbstones at Newgrange, Knowth and Dowth paired with Atlantic island genomic affinities (UNESCO WHC 659).
evidence.summary: Boyne Valley passage graves combine drystone corbelled roofs, roof-box winter solstice illumination and spiral megalithic art linked across Irish Sea and Orcadian communities.
evidence.limits: Complex reuse spanning Beaker and Iron Age activity requires careful stratigraphic separation.

evidence.title: Pontic–Caspian Steppe to Central European Corded Ware: Horse pastoralism & 3rd-millennium turnover
evidence.dateBasis: Ancient autosomal and Y-chromosome genomes paired with kurgan burials, battle axes and wheeled-wagon pastoral economies.
evidence.summary: Steppe pastoralists expanded westward into Corded Ware and Bell Beaker horizons after c. 3000 BCE, transforming European ancestry profiles alongside copper-arsenic metallurgy and steppe wheeled herding.
evidence.limits: Genetic turnover rates differed markedly between continental lowlands and Mediterranean peninsulas.

evidence.title: Knossos, Phaistos & Minoan Palatial Crete: Maritime stores, olive oil & Linear A
evidence.dateBasis: Multi-wing central courts, pithos olive-oil magazines, undeciphered Linear A administrative tablets and Cretan–Egyptian synchronisms (UNESCO WHC 1733).
evidence.summary: Crete’s Bronze Age court complexes integrated regional olive/textile craft production, Cretan Hieroglyphic and Linear A bookkeeping and long-distance copper, ivory and Cycladic exchange.
evidence.limits: Undeciphered Linear A leaves internal Minoan political terminology and language family unresolved.

evidence.title: Mycenae, Tiryns & Palace of Nestor at Pylos: Cyclopean citadels & Linear B archives
evidence.dateBasis: Fired Linear B clay tablets reading archaic Mycenaean Greek, Griffin Warrior–era tholos/shaft tombs and Cyclopean masonry (UNESCO WHC 941).
evidence.summary: Continental Mycenaean kingdoms controlled regional perfumed oils, bronze armories, purple-dyed elite textiles and maritime redistribution until palace destructions around 1200 BCE.
evidence.limits: Baked Linear B records only capture the final administrative year before palace fires.

evidence.title: Únětice Principality & Nebra Sky Disc (Mittelberg, Saxony-Anhalt): Early Bronze tin networks
evidence.dateBasis: Geochemical tin/gold sourcing of the Nebra Sky Disc hoard alongside Únětice princely barrow metallurgy and settlement dynamics.
evidence.summary: Unites Cornish tin, Transylvanian gold and Alpine copper into Únětice central Germany’s stratified longhouse villages and the Nebra bronze–gold astronomical hoard.
evidence.limits: Single-find metal hoards outside controlled graves require multi-proxy patina and soil stratigraphy.

evidence.title: Terramare Embanked Villages (Fondo Paviani, Po Plain): Bronze Age northern Italian hydraulic grids
evidence.dateBasis: Remote sensing, LiDAR and borehole geophysics revealing moated geometric village layouts and Alpine–Aegean amber/metal ties.
evidence.summary: Moat-enclosed Po Valley Terramare towns sustained intensive agriculture and bronze foundry production bridging Central Europe, amber corridors and Mycenaean–Adriatic ports.
evidence.limits: Intensive modern Po Valley plowing truncates upper earthen banks across non-moated interiors.

evidence.title: Nuragic Sardinia & Tyrrhenian Metal Trade: Dry-stone towers & Nordic–Levantine copper networks
evidence.dateBasis: Viewshed GIS of >7,000 nuraghi stone towers and trace-element/lead-isotope provenance of Sardinian, Cypriot and Scandinavian bronzes.
evidence.summary: Sardinia’s Nuragic builders erected thousands of monumental drystone towers and sacred water sanctuaries while brokering Mediterranean–Atlantic tin and copper ingots.
evidence.limits: Multi-century tower rebuilds complicate pinning initial foundation dates for unexcavated nuraghi.

evidence.title: Tollense Valley Battlefield (Mecklenburg): Large-scale Northern Bronze Age warfare
evidence.dateBasis: Direct AMS bone dates and strontium/aDNA assays on >140 fighters preserved in anoxic river-peat sediments near an excavated timber causeway.
evidence.summary: Preserves Europe’s earliest large-scale battlefield where hundreds of armed men with flint/bronze arrowheads and wooden clubs clashed across a river causeway.
evidence.limits: Alluvial river migration scatters disarticulated skeletal clusters downstream.

evidence.title: El Argar & La Almoloya (Southeastern Iberia): Stratified Bronze Age silver-diadem polities
evidence.dateBasis: AMS-dated intramural jar/cist burials, frontier ceramic distribution and silver–copper–gold grave wealth in Murcia–Almería.
evidence.summary: Shows early western Mediterranean hereditary stratification where hilltop terraced towns monopolized Iberian silver ores, halberds and cereal Tribute storage.
evidence.limits: Collapse around 1550 BCE leaves sudden post-Argaric frontier rural settlement sparser.

evidence.title: Heuneburg Citadel & Early Celtic Elites (Upper Danube): Mudbrick walls & dynastic tumuli
evidence.dateLabel: c. 750–400 BCE (Hallstatt D – Early La Tène)
evidence.dateBasis: Ancient genomes from Eberdingen-Hochdorf and Magdalenenberg paired with block-excavated Keltenblock chamber burials and Attic imports.
evidence.summary: Genetic pedigree reconstruction shows Early Celtic central European elites inherited high-status tumulus power across maternal–paternal aristocratic lineages connected to Massalia Greek wine trade.
evidence.limits: Acidic grave fills spare elite timber chambers while eroding lower-status flat cemeteries.

evidence.title: Cerveteri & Etruscan Maritime City-States (Tyrrhenian Italy): Urban grids & chamber necropoleis
evidence.dateBasis: Tufa-carved noble tomb families, coastal emporia at Pyrgi (Punic–Etruscan gold tablets) and Iron Age–Orientalizing urban surveys.
evidence.summary: Illuminates urbanized Etruscan aristocratic cities exporting iron, grain and bucchero wares across Tyrrhenian networks while adopting Phoenician–Greek alphabetical literacy.
evidence.limits: Sub-urban modern agriculture obscures timber/mudbrick domestic quarters compared to monumental tufa tombs.

evidence.title: Scythian Kurgans & Forest-Steppe Citadels (Bilsk & North Pontic): Pastoral–agrarian Iron Age steppe
evidence.dateBasis: Mound visibility surveys, Black Sea Greek amphora trade and fortified earthwork mega-settlements across Ukrainian–Don forest-steppe.
evidence.summary: Demonstrates that Pontic–Scythian Iron Age society combined mounted steppe pastoralism and royal kurgan landscapes with vast fortified forest-steppe artisanal hubs like Bilsk.
evidence.limits: Antiquarian looting of royal kurgan chambers fragments original contextual associations.

evidence.title: Classical–Hellenistic Poleis: Athens Acropolis, Delphi & Olympia pan-Mediterranean civic hubs
evidence.dateBasis: Multi-settlement geophysical surveys, polis urban sightline modeling, Attic/Corinthian epigraphy and UNESCO sanctuary archives (WHC 404, 393, 517).
evidence.summary: Traces emergence of alphabetic civic poleis, pan-Hellenic sanctuaries at Delphi and Olympia, Classical marble architecture on the Athenian Acropolis and Mediterranean-Black Sea colonial networks.
evidence.limits: Monumental stone sanctuaries are far denser in the archaeological record than rural slave and tenant farmsteads.

evidence.title: Rome, Ostia Antica & Pompeii: Republican–Imperial Roman streets, port warehouses & civic life
evidence.dateBasis: 79 CE Vesuvian volcanic sealing at Pompeii and Herculaneum alongside brick-stamped insulae and Portus harbors at Ostia (UNESCO WHC 91, 829).
evidence.summary: Connects imperial Rome’s monumental marble fora and Trajanic–Claudian grain harbors at Ostia with Pompeii’s intact bakeries, elections painted on plaster walls and shop-lined thoroughfares.
evidence.limits: 79 CE Vesuvian eruption freezes a first-century Campanian snapshot while Late Antique imperial shifts appear most vividly at Rome and Ostia.

evidence.title: Carnuntum (Danube Limes, Austria): Legionary frontier metropolis, governor palace & ludus
evidence.dateBasis: Ground-penetrating radar and magnetometry mapping the Pannonia Superior capital, amphitheaters and the intact gladiatorial training school.
evidence.summary: Non-invasive prospection across Carnuntum reveals how Roman legionary fortresses generated bilingual frontier cities uniting Germanic–Danubian traders, imperial command and veteran farms.
evidence.limits: Sub-meter geophysical reconstructions require targeted excavation trenches to date discrete demolition floors.

evidence.title: Ravenna & Adriatic Sea Gateways: Late Roman capital to Byzantine Exarchate mosaics
evidence.dateBasis: Standing brick-and-Proconnesian-marble basilicas, baptisteries and harbor stratigraphy at Classe linking western Italy to Constantinople (UNESCO WHC 788).
evidence.summary: Illustrates early-medieval Mediterranean urban continuity where Ravenna and port Classe funneled eastern Roman ceramics, silk, mosaic artisans and diplomacy across northern Italy.
evidence.limits: Prograding Po Delta siltation buried parts of ancient Classe’s harbor quays.

evidence.title: Córdoba, Medina Azahara & Granada (Al-Andalus): Umayyad–Nasrid irrigated cities & scholarship
evidence.dateBasis: Urban stratigraphy, hydraulic norias, Great Mosque of Córdoba (WHC 313) and Nasrid Alhambra palaces/restoration archives (WHC 314).
evidence.summary: Traces Iberian Islamic urbanization uniting citrus/rice irrigation, multilingual translation workshops, ceramic lusterware industries and architectural synthesis across Umayyad Córdoba through Nasrid Granada.
evidence.limits: Medieval–early modern cathedral and palace conversions reshaped portions of inner urban street grids.

evidence.title: Veliki Preslav, Pliska & Zalavár/Mosapurc: First Bulgarian Empire & Central-SE Slavic polities
evidence.dateBasis: Geophysical prospection of Veliki Preslav royal compounds, Zalavár island churches and Great Moravian fortified centres at Pohansko.
evidence.summary: Reveals rapid seventh–tenth-century state formation across Slavic and Bulgar realms, adopting Cyrillic–Glagolitic literacy, monumental stone palaces and Byzantine–Carolingian prestige exchange.
evidence.limits: Earthen ramparts and reused Roman spolia mask early wooden aristocratic compounds.

evidence.title: Staraya Ladoga, Novgorod & Kyivan Rus’: Amber–silver river arteries to Old Rus’ brick cathedrals
evidence.dateBasis: Dendrochronology of Novgorod’s waterlogged log streets, birchbark vernacular letters, Staraya Ladoga beads and Kyivan arch-gabled masonry.
evidence.summary: Captures Baltic–Dnieper–Volga river connectivity linking Scandinavian–Finno-Ugric–Slavic nodal emporia into literate Christian Rus’ cities famous for vernacular birchbark correspondence.
evidence.limits: Twelfth-century stone churches fared much better than Mongol-era outer timber districts.

evidence.title: Carolingian–Ottonian Heartland (Aachen–Rhine–Loire): Monastic estates, palaces & early chartered towns
evidence.dateBasis: Excavations of royal palaces (Pfalzen), rural peasant estates, cathedral precincts and comparative historic-town atlases across Western Europe.
evidence.summary: Documents demographic expansion under manorial agriculture, Benedictine–Carolingian scriptoria and renewed silver denier coinage that launched high-medieval chartered urban growth.
evidence.limits: Continuous later urban construction deeply truncates earliest Carolingian timber burgage plots.

evidence.title: Palermo, Monreale & Norman Sicily: Trilingual Latin–Greek–Arabic Mediterranean crown
evidence.dateBasis: Comparative town charters, Norman monastic land registers (Chiesazza) and royal Palermo Arab-Norman palace–cathedral architecture.
evidence.summary: Synthesizes Islamic agronomy, Greek Byzantine mosaics and Latin feudal administration inside twelfth-century Sicily alongside Western European communal guild and parish towns.
evidence.limits: Chancery records heavily privilege royal, monastic and merchant elites over rural laborers.

evidence.title: Florence, Venice Lagoon, Lisbon & Seville: Renaissance–early modern global oceanic emporia
evidence.dateBasis: Excavated early-modern ceramics, Lisbon–Seville Casa de la Contratación records, Florentine merchant archives and Venice Lagoon heritage (WHC 394).
evidence.summary: Maps Europe’s pivot from Italian Mediterranean city-republics and banking houses toward Atlantic-facing Iberian capitals funneling American silver, spices and global botanical transfers.
evidence.limits: Archival wealth outpaces subsurface excavations across dense living historic cores except after urban renewal.

evidence.title: Amsterdam Canal Ring & North Sea Entrepôts: Land reclamation & 17th-century global consumer material
evidence.dateBasis: Metro-line and harbor-fill urban excavations yielding porcelain, clay tobacco pipes, tropical woods and merchant household waste.
evidence.summary: Waterlogged reclamation landfills around Amsterdam preserve thousands of everyday global artifacts—from Ming/Jingdezhen sherds to American tobacco pipes—tracking mercantile consumerism.
evidence.limits: Reclaimed dump contexts blend secondary domestic refuse across decades.

evidence.title: Ironbridge Gorge & Manchester (Britain): Coke iron-smelting, steam textiles & Industrial Revolution to 1900
evidence.dateBasis: Excavated Coalbrookdale coke blast furnaces (1709), the 1779 Iron Bridge (UNESCO WHC 371) and pre-1806 Manchester steam-engine foundations.
evidence.summary: Traces Europe’s fossil-fuel industrial watershed from Darby’s Coalbrookdale coke smelting and Severn valley workers’ cottages to Manchester’s rotary steam cotton mills and rail networks up to 1900.
evidence.limits: Industrial heritage conservation disproportionately preserves monumental bridges and grand mills relative to demolished worker terraces.

evidence.title: St. Petersburg & Baltic Industrialization (1703–1900): Planned imperial harbor & factory complexes
evidence.dateBasis: Industrial-archaeological architectural inventories of Admiralty shipyards, Obvodny Canal brick textile mills and Imperial Porcelain manufactures.
evidence.summary: Documents continental industrialization in Eastern Europe as St. Petersburg coupled planned marsh-reclamation canals and Baltic maritime shipyards with nineteenth-century mechanical manufacturing to 1900.
evidence.limits: Twentieth-century factory conversions erased segments of nineteenth-century timber worker suburbs.

waves.title: Neolithic Agropastoral Dispersal via Aegean–Balkan Loess & Cardial Sea Routes
waves.dateBasis: Connects Franchthi, Middle Struma, Lepenski Vir, Central European LBK wells and Cardial coastal sequences with genomic transects.
waves.summary: Schematic dual dispersal pathways illustrating Anatolian–Aegean farmers expanding rapidly along riverine Danubian loess plains (LBK) and by boat along Cardial Mediterranean–Atlantic coasts.
waves.limits: Generalized overland and coastal vectors simplify nuanced centuries-long frontier pauses and hunter-gatherer admixtures.

waves.title: Steppe Yamnaya Mobility & Bronze Age Amber–Tin–Copper Trade Networks
waves.dateBasis: Synthesizes Pontic–Danubian aDNA transitions, Nebra metallurgical provenance and Baltic–Nuragic–Mycenaean bronze trade signatures.
waves.summary: Tracks third-to-second-millennium steppe pastoralist westward mobility followed by pan-European bronze alloy trade connecting Baltic amber, Cornish/Erzgebirge tin, Alpine–Cypriot copper and Aegean palaces.
waves.limits: Routes merge multiple asynchronous mobility and long-distance exchange episodes.

waves.title: Classical Poleis, Roman Limes, Rus’ River Corridors & Atlantic–Industrial Transformation
waves.dateBasis: Unites Classical Athens/Rome/Carnuntum infrastructure, Novgorod–Kyiv river trade, Italian–Iberian oceanic entrepôts and Ironbridge–Manchester steam networks.
waves.summary: Schematic urban corridor tracing Europe’s multi-millennial civic integration from Mediterranean stone poleis and Imperial Roman frontiers to riverine Rus’ towns, Atlantic maritime hubs and industrial steam networks through 1900.
waves.limits: Schematic backbone cannot show localized wars, plagues or regional rural continuities.
